title: Biologist 1 (Wildlife) / Trainee 1 & 2 — NY HELPS, no exam required
org: NYS Office of Parks, Recreation & Historic Preservation · Division of Environmental Stewardship & Planning · Albany, NY
benefits: New York State employee benefits — health, dental, NYSLRS retirement, paid leave
metaLine: Closes Aug 13 · PERMANENT state wildlife biologist · trainee levels let a BS substitute for experience
body: A permanent wildlife biologist position in the Wildlife Unit of the Division of Environmental Stewardship and Planning, applying ecological and conservation-biology principles across the New York State Park system. Duties include on-the-ground stewardship projects, rare, threatened and endangered species conservation, habitat inventory and condition documentation, and habitat-connectivity planning. Advertised with Trainee 1 and 2 levels under NY HELPS, so no civil service exam is required.
desc: The trainee levels under NY HELPS are the whole point: they let a bachelor's degree substitute for the experience a permanent state biologist post would normally demand, and no civil service exam stands in the way. This is a permanent, benefited wildlife biologist job she can genuinely qualify for right now — apply at the trainee level, not the full grade.

title: Research Scientist 1 (Water Pollution) — statewide monitoring and HABs
org: NYS Department of Environmental Conservation · Bureau of Water Assessment and Management · Albany, NY
location: Albany, New York (statewide lakes and streams)
benefits: New York State employee benefits — health, dental, NYSLRS retirement, paid leave
metaLine: Closes Aug 26 · $66,951 start · NON-COMPETITIVE — no civil service exam · her capstone subject exactly
body: A contingent-permanent, non-competitive scientist role in the Monitoring and Assessment Section supporting statewide lake and stream water-quality programmes. Half the position is applied research and data analysis on harmful algal blooms and the Lake Classification and Inventory Program, including collecting, analysing and interpreting water-quality data statewide. Non-competitive class means no civil service exam is required.
desc: Statewide water-quality monitoring and data analysis is the exact subject area of her contamination capstone, and the non-competitive classification removes the exam barrier that blocks most New York state science jobs. At nearly $67,000 starting, this is the highest-paying genuinely-reachable position found in the Northeast this run.

title: Resource Conservation Technician — erosion, sediment and stream/wetland projects
org: Elk County Conservation District · Saint Marys, PA
url_label: TAMU board — Elk County Conservation District 117651
benefits: Full benefits package including healthcare and retirement
metaLine: Closes Aug 14 · full benefits · stream and wetland conservation + erosion/sediment permitting · NO experience required
body: A full-time county conservation district technician working on erosion and sediment control, stormwater management, permitting, and stream and wetland conservation projects across Elk County. Minimum education is an associate degree in a natural resources field or equivalent combination, with no prior experience required. Includes a full benefits package with healthcare and retirement.
desc: Stream and wetland conservation combined with erosion and sediment permitting is a near-perfect use of her Army Corps wetland delineation training, and sediment delivery to streams is the precise process she studied after Hurricane Helene. The salary is modest but it is a full-time benefited position with no experience barrier.

title: Fish and Wildlife Technician 1 — Snapshot NY camera-trap project
org: NYS Department of Environmental Conservation, Region 2 · Long Island City (Queens), NY
benefits: Confirm the seasonal appointment terms with the department
metaLine: Closes Aug 20 · the preferred qualifications match her resume line for line
body: A seasonal technician supporting Snapshot NY, a statewide trail-camera species inventory, in New York City's Region 2. Duties include landowner coordination, deploying, retrieving and servicing trail cameras, and processing and organising photo data, plus assisting with other regional wildlife surveys and Wildlife Health Program carcass collection. Preferred qualifications explicitly list prior trail-camera handling, urban ecology and mammal coursework, and GPS navigation.
desc: This is the rare posting where the preferred-qualifications list reads like her resume: prior trail-camera handling, mammal coursework and GPS navigation are all things she can evidence. Her Wildlife Insights experience makes the photo-processing half of the job familiar too. The pay is seasonal-technician level, so treat it as a credential and a foot in the door at DEC.

title: Fisheries Biologist 1 — northwest Pennsylvania
org: Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission · Linesville, PA
location: Linesville, Pennsylvania (northwest PA lakes, rivers and streams)
benefits: Commonwealth of Pennsylvania employee benefits — health, retirement, paid leave
metaLine: ⚠️ Closes Aug 12 · $53,008 · BIOLOGIST title, bachelor's-level with NO experience required
body: An entry-grade fisheries management biologist for northwest Pennsylvania, running field studies on lakes, rivers and streams and leading field crews. Duties include data entry and analysis in the Agency Resource Database, fish age and growth analysis, angler creel surveys, and drafting reports. The role also assists with fish kill and pollution event investigations.
desc: Bachelor's-level with no experience required, carrying the biologist title, at $53,000 — and the pollution-event investigation duties tie straight back to her trace-metal contamination work. It closes August 12, so this is a two-day window.

title: Field Technician — Center for Clean Water Technology
org: Stony Brook University · Center for Clean Water Technology · Stony Brook, NY
location: Stony Brook, New York (field sites across Long Island)
url_label: Conservation Job Board — Stony Brook Field Technician
benefits: Stony Brook University employee benefits — confirm the package
metaLine: Closes Aug 20 · $47,000–$50,000 PERMANENT · water sampling + BOD5 and suspended solids lab work
body: A permanent technician collecting water samples from experimental nitrogen-removing treatment systems across Long Island and recording onsite field measurements. The role also runs laboratory analyses including BOD5 and suspended solids, coordinates sampling schedules, supervises graduate students, and handles data entry and site reporting, supporting efforts to improve Long Island drinking and groundwater quality.
desc: Water-quality field sampling paired with laboratory analysis is her exact capstone skill set, and this one is permanent rather than seasonal. Being embedded at a university centre also puts her next to a graduate department while she is deciding — and supervising graduate students is a genuine leadership line for an application.

title: Environmental Analyst — NPDES Permit Writer
org: NEIWPCC, placed at NYSDEC · Albany, NY
url_label: Conservation Job Board — NEIWPCC Permit Writer
benefits: NEIWPCC employee benefits — confirm the package
metaLine: Closes Aug 23 · $60,000–$70,000 · explicitly framed as a chance to LEARN environmental compliance
body: A full-time analyst developing permits that control discharges of pollutants to surface water and groundwater, embedded in the Drinking Water Source Protection Program. The work involves engaging with permittees, engineers and the public on municipal and industrial permitting, and the posting explicitly frames it as an opportunity to learn environmental compliance. NEIWPCC places staff at state agencies across the Northeast.
desc: A posting that says outright it is a place to learn compliance is unusually honest about being open to someone without the credential yet, and NPDES permit-writing turns her water-quality interest into a regulatory qualification that transfers to every state and to EPA. The NEIWPCC placement model also means the role sits inside NYSDEC without requiring a civil service exam.

title: Biologist I — Great Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve
org: New Hampshire Fish and Game Department · Marine Division · Greenland, NH
benefits: State of New Hampshire employee benefits · renewable every two years
metaLine: Closes Aug 20 · vegetation + wildlife + water quality in ONE job — the three threads of her degree
body: A full-time Biologist I (position 52221) collecting and analysing vegetation, wildlife, fish and water quality data through field and lab work at the Great Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve. The work tracks short- and long-term change in estuarine conditions. 37.5 hours weekly, renewable every two years.
desc: Very few postings ask for vegetation, wildlife and water-quality monitoring together — this one does, which means her whole degree is relevant rather than half of it. Great Bay is also a National Estuarine Research Reserve, so the monitoring feeds a national long-term dataset rather than sitting in a filing cabinet.

title: Surface Mine Conservation Inspector Trainee

url_label: PA NEOGOV — Surface Mine Conservation Inspector Trainee
benefits: Commonwealth of Pennsylvania employee benefits — health, retirement, paid leave

body: An explicit trainee-class DEP position learning surface mine inspection and reclamation oversight across western Pennsylvania. Duties include gathering site information, speaking with landowners, and supporting responsible mining practices and public safety near active mining areas. The posting is framed as a way to begin an environmental career.
desc: Trainee-class titles are worth hunting for specifically because they are written for people without experience, and this one pays nearly $47,000 to start. Mine reclamation is also where metals enter watersheds in the first place, which connects it directly to her trace-metal capstone.

body: 1,700-hour AmeriCorps service positions with a network of more than thirty land conservation and sustainable agriculture non-profits across Massachusetts. Members choose from five coordinator tracks including Land Stewardship Coordinator and Land Conservation Coordinator, and are paired with a site supervisor for mentorship. The 2026–27 programme runs September 8, 2026 to July 30, 2027.
desc: At up to $27,750 plus a $7,395 education award, this is the best-compensated service term found anywhere this run — well above the usual corps living allowance. As an NCCC alumna she can slot straight into the Land Stewardship or Land Conservation track, and a second education award would meaningfully offset graduate tuition.

body: A single position contributing to the biology programme at Cape May National Wildlife Refuge under the mentorship of refuge staff. Cape May provides critical habitat for migratory birds along the Jersey Shore. Direct mentorship from refuge biologists is also the relationship that turns into a reference and a tip-off when a permanent position opens.
